ownership.fixed: The program owns contract_ref, read_only, schema definitions, descriptions, policies, registry and source constraints. Neither model may edit these.
ownership.editable: The compiler returns ONLY the values object: requirements, assumptions, discovery, selection_authority and delivery_manifest, using the instantiated compiler output schema. It may add array rows using the item templates. Null placeholders must be filled where the output schema requires a value.
ownership.reviewer: Review the program-merged filled template against the admitted IntentIR and this same contract. Return only the reviewer output schema. Do not modify values, invent policies or redesign the workflow. Treat discovery values as instructions for future execution after planning, not as claims that candidates already exist before Planner admission.

field_definitions./requirements: Atomic, checkable requirements with complete Intent source coverage. Their number is model-authored, not preselected by a script.
field_definitions./requirements/*/source_refs: IDs of original goals, outcomes, constraints, unknowns, ambiguities or conflicts supporting this requirement. Do not invent IDs.
field_definitions./requirements/*/priority: Preserve the user's strength. A preference is not automatically a must. Runtime validity policies must not be rewritten as user-authored must requirements.
field_definitions./requirements/*/semantic_role: research_scope covers evidence subjects/selection; process covers how work proceeds; delivery covers requested output; outcome covers the requested result; resolution covers unknowns/conflicts; constraint covers other restrictions. Preserve original meaning, not merely the spelling of the source category.
field_definitions./requirements/*/acceptance: Checkable acceptance criteria, not automatically search keywords. scope_coverage is only for research_scope; process and delivery criteria must not become source-topic filters.
field_definitions./requirements/*/check: Choose exactly one ID from read_only.requirement_check_options. These checks evaluate whether a future bound output satisfies this requirement. Do not select an artifact_type check: artifact-schema checks are attached automatically only after the Planner chooses a compatible output ABI. In particular, a workflow Evidence Gate or Closure condition is not an artifact_review.v1 requirement, and a pre-draft report-plan review is not a final artifact review. A check name containing constraint_coverage does not override semantic_role. Do not demand an unregistered check.
field_definitions./selection_authority: One entry per hard retrieval restriction: /discovery/inclusion_criteria/<index>, /discovery/exclusion_criteria/<index>, /discovery/coverage/<index>/required when true, non-null /discovery/time_range/start_year or end_year, and /discovery/minimum_candidates when greater than the runtime floor. Cite exact Intent IDs and explain explicit source-selection authority. An explicit lower bound on the total sources or evidence corpus used by the workflow may authorize the same lower bound on accepted discovery candidates when those sources must pass through this discovery/ingestion path. This is a necessary upstream execution condition, not proof that the final deliverable already satisfies its source requirement. No entries for query strategy or required=false coverage. The program checks references and exact target coverage; the reviewer checks whether cited Intent actually supports the restriction. Do not manufacture authority to satisfy validation.
field_definitions./requirements/*/checkable: Fixed true by the output schema. A model cannot change this constant.
field_definitions./requirements/*/disposition: Fixed null by the output schema.
field_definitions./assumptions: Explicit assumptions, not permission to invent user scope, mandatory deliverable content, source counts or scientific claims.
field_definitions./delivery_manifest: A table-like artifact for future file production. Fill it only when the user explicitly requests named files or an exact file set; otherwise use null. It is a production contract, not evidence that files already exist. Preserve every requested filename, extension, output directory, per-file purpose, count and structural constraint. Do not collapse multiple requested files into one report and do not add placeholder files.
field_definitions./delivery_manifest/output_root: The exact output directory requested by the user, stored as a safe relative path. Do not silently replace it with a generic publication directory. Machine-specific absolute prefixes are bound later by the workspace authority.
field_definitions./delivery_manifest/files/*/relative_path: The exact path beneath output_root. One row represents one required file. Do not combine, rename, omit or invent user-requested files.
field_definitions./delivery_manifest/files/*/media_type: The file's real serialization type, consistent with its extension. Markdown, CSV, JSON, HTML and plain text remain distinct contracts.
field_definitions./delivery_manifest/files/*/content_requi: All user-stated semantic requirements for this specific file, copied without weakening. These guide the semantic producer and remain subject to evidence honesty.
field_definitions./delivery_manifest/files/*/required_fiel: Exact CSV columns or JSON field names explicitly enumerated by the user. Preserve their spelling and order. Use an empty array when no machine-readable fields were specified.
field_definitions./delivery_manifest/files/*/source_refs: Exact Intent IDs that authorize this file and its contents. Do not cite unrelated research-scope requirements merely to populate the field.
field_definitions./discovery: Structured source retrieval instructions for future execution when new source discovery is needed; otherwise null. Discovery occurs after planning. Its filled values do not assert that sources or candidates already exist before Planner admission. This is not a DAG or operator selection.
field_definitions./discovery/subject: Research subject matter only. Workflow instructions, report titles/formats, evidence auditability and provenance are not source topics.
field_definitions./discovery/search_queries: Bounded complementary queries for the research subject, including useful alternatives. They are not final-report text.
field_definitions./discovery/inclusion_criteria: All criteria must match a candidate. any_of is a list of case-insensitive literal alternatives in the named field. Add a criterion only when an explicit source selection requirement supports it.
field_definitions./discovery/exclusion_criteria: Any matching criterion excludes a candidate. Preserve real user exclusions and polarity; never turn an exclusion into positive coverage. Source references must support the criterion.
field_definitions./discovery/coverage: Coverage is measured across the accepted corpus, not separately for every candidate. any_of contains literal synonyms. required=true only for explicit must-have shortlist coverage, not merely a desire for comprehensive final analysis. A request to study several methods keeps ALL methods mandatory in report acceptance; it normally uses complementary searches and required=false corpus coverage, NOT a rule requiring every paper to name those methods. Never delete report requirements to make discovery easier. Best-effort gaps remain limitations under the evidence_honesty policy.
field_definitions./review/errors: Each defect names an existing fidelity rule, a JSON pointer into the values object (or the parent collection for a missing row), supporting Intent IDs and/or declared policy IDs, and a substantive reason. accepted=true requires an empty errors array. Structured references make review auditable; they do not replace semantic judgment.
field_definitions./discovery/time_range: User-specified publication date limits. Unknown bounds stay null; do not invent dates.
field_definitions./discovery/minimum_candidates: Effective minimum number of accepted candidates required when future Discovery completes successfully. It is not a precondition that must already be satisfied before Requirement or Planner admission, and it does not claim that this many candidates currently exist. It is not identical to the final report's target source count; however, an explicit final source/corpus lower bound may authorize the same candidate lower bound when every final source must enter through this discovery/ingestion path. The candidate minimum is only a necessary upstream condition: satisfying it does not establish final-report completeness or scientific quality. Apply the named runtime validity policy below.
field_definitions./read_only/source_constraints: The exact copy of ALL original Intent constraints: polarity, category, expression AST and source spans. The name does not mean source-selection-only constraints. The program owns this copy; workflow/delivery constraints must remain here for provenance, but must not become discovery filters.
field_definitions./read_only/requirement_check_options: The table of check IDs selectable at the Requirement Compiler handoff, with their descriptions and rubrics. Every option applies to kind=bound_output. Artifact-type checks remain visible in the full evaluation_check_registry for provenance but are not selectable here; the Planner attaches them deterministically from the chosen output ABI.

evidence_honesty.meaning: Never present missing, weak or incomplete evidence as established coverage. Preserve discovery audit gaps through analysis and final reporting as limitations or unresolved questions. This is truthful handling of actual evidence gaps, not a user-requested new study or a mandatory generic limitations chapter.
evidence_honesty.review: This policy is program-owned and carried separately in semantic_contract.runtime_policies. Do not add it as a user requirement or reject it as invented scope. Reject claims of completeness unsupported by evidence. Report topic coverage remains mandatory; transparent gaps do not automatically establish task success.

discovery_nonempty_handoff.meaning: Zero usable candidates must not be passed to evidence-consuming downstream work as a successful discovery result. This is a runtime safety/validity floor, not an extra user requirement.
discovery_nonempty_handoff.override: Use a higher minimum when an explicit Intent requirement states a candidate lower bound or a lower bound on sources/evidence that the workflow must ultimately use and those sources must pass through this discovery/ingestion handoff. A final source lower bound may therefore authorize the same accepted-candidate lower bound even when the user did not restate the number using retrieval-stage terminology. The value governs future Discovery completion and never requires candidates to exist before Requirement or Planner admission. Account for its Intent source in discovery.source_refs, the corresponding requirement and selection_authority. Never invent a higher number from vague completeness language or silently weaken an explicit lower bound.
discovery_nonempty_handoff.review: With no user count, minimum_candidates=1 is required by this contract and is not an invented user count. Do not demand null, zero or removal. When the Intent explicitly requires N total sources/evidence items and they enter through this discovery/ingestion path, minimum_candidates=N is a supported necessary upstream condition; do not reject it merely because the Intent phrases N as a final corpus or report requirement. This does not prove the final artifact uses N valid sources. An explicit continue-on-provider-failure instruction governs degraded workflow continuation separately and does not erase the normal successful-discovery minimum.

fidelity_rules.description: Account for every Intent goal, outcome, constraint, unknown, ambiguity and conflict through source_refs. Preserve project identity, requested deliverables and the timing of required resolutions.

Preserve polarity, category meaning and strength. Do not turn preferences into musts, exclusions into positive coverage, or unspecified scope/date/count into user requirements. Apply explicitly declared runtime policies as runtime policies, not as user requests.
Keep process, delivery and evidence topics separate. User workflow instructions remain requirements but are not source selection or lexical coverage criteria.

Use faithful, executable retrieval predicates with source-supported inclusions/exclusions and useful synonyms. Respect corpus-level coverage semantics and retain missing best-effort coverage as limitations.
Use compatible registered checks. Do not add mandatory deliverable content, extra research or policies absent from Intent and this contract. Do not design a DAG or choose operators.

Review editable values, not the program-owned contract. A genuine fidelity defect must be reported and must not be waived to make a run pass. Accept only if no substantive defects remain; when rejecting, identify the violated rule/field and the supporting Intent evidence.

When the user explicitly requests named files, delivery_manifest must preserve the exact file set, output root, formats, per-file content requirements and machine-readable fields. It must not assert that future files already exist.
